semantic_argument: The source bounds the success probability of size-bounded ARSDH circuits. The before arsdhAssumption quantifies all functions of type arsdhAdversary, without any computational-resource or adversary-class restriction.

The root condition pairing(g1,g2)≠0 implies g2≠1. In a prime-order group, exponentiation τ↦g2^τ by a nonidentity g2 is injective. The SRS publishes g2^τ, so an unrestricted function can recover τ by inverting this map.
The root premise p≥n+2 ensures that at least n+1 field elements remain after excluding τ. The adversary chooses a set S of size n+1 avoiding τ, so Z_S(τ)=∏_{s∈S}(τ-s)≠0.
Output (S,h1,h2)=(S,g1,g1^(1/Z_S(τ))). Together with hg1:g1≠1, this satisfies every arsdhCondition requirement. It succeeds for every sampled τ, giving ARSDH success probability 1.

Thus the before hardness premise cannot hold when arsdhError<1; when error≥1 it gives only a trivial probability bound. This differs from the source's computational-hardness assumption for bounded-size circuits.
The source also explicitly requires t_ARSDH ≤ t_FC + 2L² + L + D(L+8) + 2(D+1)². The formal root and related adversary and reduction definitions do not express this circuit-size guarantee.

The structure of the function-binding success event corresponds to the source, and both statements use probability inequalities. The probability-equality issue from the preceding evaluation-binding reductions is not used here.
